# .github

## What it is

`.github/` holds the repo's GitHub Actions surface: the CI parameter file `ci-config.env`, the workflow definitions under `workflows/` (PR/push CI, nightly full-CI backstop, GHCR image build + retention, release), and the issue/PR templates. Every job runs on **self-hosted Linux runners** (Hetzner, provisioned by `scripts/provision/setup-runner-native.sh`) — there are no GitHub-hosted runners on this repo. A single `changes` job per workflow computes per-run flags from the event.

## Core responsibilities

### `ci-config.env` — the single versioned source of CI parameters (S1)

CI frequency and cost parameters live only in `.github/ci-config.env`; changing them means editing the file and opening a PR (reviewed, traceable — no runtime tuning; the single-owner PR loop is fast enough). Workflows read it with a **parse-and-export loader** that extracts `KEY=VALUE` lines and never executes file content — a first-day incident (`NIGHTLY_CRON=0 17 * * *` run by `source` → "17: command not found", exit 127 on every push:main) replaced `source` with a `while read` loop; non-assignment lines warn and are skipped. A missing file fails the `changes` job loudly rather than silently defaulting; every read site also carries a `${VAR:-default}` fallback whose default is the safer direction (more full CI, never less).

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `FULL_CI_EVERY_N_COMMITS` | 100 | push:main runs full CI every N commits (see S2) |
| `E2E_SAMPLE_RATE_PCT` | 30 | % of non-full, non-e2e-trigger PRs that run e2e |
| `NIGHTLY_ENABLED` | true | nightly full-CI backstop master switch |
| `NIGHTLY_FLAKY_RETRIES` | 2 | retries for flaky suites in nightly (PR CI never retries) |

`NIGHTLY_CRON` exists as a commented documentation line only — GitHub Actions `schedule` cron must be a literal in `nightly.yml`; changing the time means editing both files.

### `workflows/ci.yml` — PR + push CI with tiered frequency (S1/S2)

- **PRs (diff-driven, 2026-08-05 budget ruling)**: the `changes` job diffs against the base ref and sets `backend` / `frontend` / `full` / `e2e` flags from path groups. Docs-only PRs run just the `docs-only` gate; unknown paths, CI-infra changes (`.github/`, `scripts/`, `Dockerfile`, `.mergify.yml`, …), and cross-stack changes always go full.
- **e2e sampling (S1)**: a PR that is neither full nor e2e-trigger runs e2e with probability `E2E_SAMPLE_RATE_PCT`, decided **deterministically** by `md5(commit sha) % 100 < PCT` — the same commit always samples the same way, reproducible and debuggable. e2e-trigger contract paths (timeline/marker wiring, `tests/e2e/` — Task #1018) ignore sampling and always run.
- **push:main sampling (S2)**: full CI on main no longer runs on every merge. The `changes` job computes `git rev-list --count HEAD % FULL_CI_EVERY_N_COMMITS` — stateless, deterministic, monotonic on main; large PRs (more commits) hit more often, matching "bigger change → deserves full CI". Non-hit merges skip every job (workflow green, no check reported): Mergify already re-ran PR CI on the rebased head, so the combined state was verified, and nightly covers the gaps. Before sampling the job unshallows history — a shallow `rev-list` under-counts, and a count below 1000 fails loudly rather than silently skipping forever.
- **workflow_dispatch / merge_group**: always full CI, no sampling.
- Jobs: `backend-parallel` (pytest stable + coverage), `backend-serial` (lint + pyright + flaky), `frontend` (eslint + tsc + vitest), `desktop` (electron syntax + lockfile), `e2e` (Playwright happy path), and the `backend` aggregate gate that judges the two halves (`success|skipped` allow-list). Job **names are a frozen contract** — `.mergify.yml` merge_conditions match by exact name (see Notes).

### `workflows/nightly.yml` — full-CI backstop (L3)

Daily at **17:00 UTC** (Beijing 01:00 — user's deep sleep, off the PR-CI runner contention) it runs the same job set as ci.yml — backend-parallel, backend-serial, frontend, desktop, e2e, backend aggregate gate — copied **verbatim**, with two differences: the `changes` job always outputs all-true (no path filtering on a full run), and the flaky suites (pytest `-m flaky`, `vitest.flaky.config.ts`) retry `NIGHTLY_FLAKY_RETRIES` times at shell level (no plugin). It is the confidence baseline for the sampling scheme: it catches cross-merge combination bugs (each PR green, main red) and covers sampled-out merges. `workflow_call` reuse was deliberately deferred — a called workflow's job names get a `<caller> /` prefix that would break `.mergify.yml` exact-name matching.

### Other workflows

- `build-image.yml` — rebuild + push the unified image to `ghcr.io/<owner>/ava`. Since 2026-08-05 CI jobs run directly on self-hosted runners (no `container:`), so the image has **no CI consumer**; kept for manual rebuilds only (`workflow_dispatch`).
- `ghcr-retention.yml` — weekly (Mondays 04:00 UTC) prune of orphaned GHCR image versions; dry-run input available.
- `release.yml` — a dated three-segment tag push creates a GitHub Release with the tag's annotation as body (written by `scripts/release_cut.py`).

## Key dependencies

- [[../scripts/scripts.ava.okf.md]] — `scripts/provision/setup-runner-native.sh` provisions the runners; `ci_utils.py` polls PR CI / enqueues merges; `release_cut.py` writes release tags.
- [[../tests/tests.ava.okf.md]] — the suite the CI gates run; the flaky markers (`pytest -m flaky`, `vitest.flaky.config.ts`) are what nightly retries.
- `.mergify.yml` — merge queue: rebases the PR, re-runs CI on the rebased head (what makes push:main sampling safe), and matches jobs by exact name.
- Self-hosted runner fleet + `/var/cache/ava-ci/` persistent caches (uv/pip/pre-commit/npm/playwright); fleet sizing in `ops/ci_autoscale/README.md`.

## Entry points

- Events: `push` (main, `paths-ignore` *.md), `pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule` (nightly), inert `merge_group`.
- Tuning CI cost/frequency: edit `.github/ci-config.env` in a PR.
- Manual full run: `workflow_dispatch` on ci.yml or nightly.yml.

## Notes

- **Job names must never change** — `.mergify.yml` `merge_conditions` match `check-success=<exact name>`; renaming a job silently unblocks merges it was meant to gate. This is why nightly.yml duplicates ci.yml verbatim instead of using `workflow_call`.
- **nightly.yml is manually synced** with ci.yml — when ci.yml's job set or steps change, nightly.yml must follow; a red nightly is often a stale copy.
- The proof-of-work tripwire (artifact upload with `if-no-files-found: error`) makes "the suite did not run" a red job — the 2026-08-05 zero-byte-uv incident's guard; it applies to both CI workflows.
- Deterministic sampling (sha modulo) is intentional: a sampled run is reproducible for a given commit, unlike a random draw.
